title: Miyoshi et al. (2026): Local Acceleration of Multi-MeV Electrons Inside Earth's Impenetrable Barrier During the May 2024 Superstorm
citation: Geophysical Research Letters 2026, doi:10.1029/2026GL125879; press release dated 2026-10-28, https://en.nagoya-u.ac.jp/news/articles/pr-2024-solar-storm-triggered-ultra-relativistic-electrons-inside-earths-impenetrable-barrier/
materials: Press release only (read through a fetch tool). Paper, figures, methods and supplement NOT read: Wiley and phys.org pages returned client errors. Independent check: arXiv:2602.03990 abstract page (CALET on the ISS, same storm), read through a fetch tool. Baker et al. 2014 (origin of the barrier) not read.
decision_context: User-chosen study. Two decisions it could feed: whether spacecraft radiation planning can treat the region inside about 3 Earth radii as protected from multi-MeV electrons, and whether radiation-belt forecast models need a local acceleration source at low L. No decision owner named.

claims.text: in 2024, Japan's Arase space probe detected these electrons well inside the barrier
claims.evidence_location: Press release; paper figures not read. Independently: CALET reports relativistic electrons down to L = 2.2, below the nominal L = 2.8 barrier, persisting months (https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03990)
claims.measurand: presence of multi-MeV (some above 3 MeV) electrons inside about 3 Earth radii
claims.falsifiers: Arase and CALET both report presence from different orbits and detectors. A shared contamination (for example penetrating protons counted as electrons) would have to affect both.
claims.label: OBSERVED
claims.instrument: Arase particle instruments (paper); CALET on the ISS (independent, integral count rates)

claims.text: the electrons were accelerated locally rather than infiltrating from outer radiation belts
claims.evidence_location: Press release: a distinct local PSD peak near the barrier boundary that strengthened over time. Method not read.
claims.measurand: radial PSD profile at fixed adiabatic invariants; growth of a local maximum
claims.falsifiers: The peak disappears or moves when PSD is recomputed with a second field model; or a transport model with fast inward injection and L-dependent loss reproduces a growing peak at the same place; or the peak is absent at other first invariants where chorus acceleration predicts it.
claims.label: DERIVED
claims.instrument: Arase electron data over several orbits, converted to PSD with a magnetic field model (model not stated in material read)

claims.text: chorus waves ... potentially providing favorable conditions
claims.evidence_location: Press release: intense rising/falling-tone chorus seen by Arase; plasmasphere slow to recover (about 4.3-4.7 days vs about 2 typical)
claims.measurand: energy transfer from chorus to multi-MeV electrons at about 3 Earth radii
claims.falsifiers: A quasi-linear or test-particle calculation with the observed chorus amplitude and density gives acceleration far too slow to build the observed peak in the observed time. Not reported in the material read.
claims.label: PROPOSED
claims.instrument: Arase wave measurements; link to acceleration by timing

claims.text: The so-called impenetrable barrier seemed to have been broken.
claims.measurand: whether multi-MeV electrons can exist inside the empirical inner boundary first reported in 2014
claims.falsifiers: The 2014 boundary was characterized over storms of a range that did not include a superstorm; if so, 'broken' and 'outside the conditions it was measured in' predict the same observation.
claims.label: DERIVED
claims.instrument: comparison of the May 2024 observation against the boundary location

tools.output: Type EMPIRICAL (single-event spacecraft observation plus interpretation). Material is a press release, so cards run on what the release states; method-level checks are NOT_CHECKED rather than passed.

4 claims. Conditional form of C2: IF the PSD peak is real in adiabatic coordinates (field-model independent) AND transport plus loss cannot build a growing peak there, THEN the electrons were accelerated locally. Neither antecedent is checkable from the release.

C1 graded MEASURED_PRESENT (direct detection, corroborated). C2 and C3 UNDECLARED: PSD depends on a field model not named in the material, and the chorus link is by timing. Two input averages, both FROZEN as stated: the barrier location (A1) and the typical recovery time (A2).

Independent route for C1: CALET on the ISS (different orbit, detector, team) sees relativistic electrons at L 2.2-3.2 for months after the storm. Supports presence, not mechanism: CALET reports count rates, not PSD. CALET's own wording ('pushed down' from the outer belt, per its plain language summary as read) is a transport reading of the same event. So: agreement on presence, the two routes differ on mechanism wording.

Open branches for the growing PSD peak: (a) local acceleration by chorus (paper); (b) fast inward transport plus L-dependent loss (hiss inside the eroded plasmasphere) leaving an apparent peak; (c) the peak is produced by the field model used to compute adiabatic coordinates during an extreme storm; (d) a mixture. Cheapest discriminator: recompute PSD with a second field model, and check the peak across several first invariants. Whether the paper ran either is not in the material read.

Term frame: 'impenetrable barrier' names an empirical boundary from observations up to 2014 and is used in the release as if it were a property of the system ('broken'). The May 2024 storm is outside the storm range that boundary was characterized on (window and population undeclared, A1). The boundary is a reading taken under earlier conditions applied under new ones.

Target: where do multi-MeV electrons inside about 3 Earth radii come from? Rendering: 'accelerated locally rather than infiltrating'. Presence is observed twice independently (C1); mechanism is an inference from one PSD profile in one storm, not checkable at press-release depth (C2).

decisions.text: Stop treating the region inside about 3 Earth radii as protected from multi-MeV electrons in spacecraft radiation planning for superstorm conditions. Depends only on C1 (presence, two instruments), not on the mechanism.
Add a local acceleration source at low L to radiation-belt forecast models? Depends on C2, which is UNDETERMINED here: needs the paper's PSD method and the field-model check (T5).

design_checks.finding: One storm (May 2024), described as a superstorm. The release reports no other event and no generalization. n = 1 event: the result is an existence observation, not a rate.

Phase space density (PSD) against radial distance requires adiabatic coordinates computed from a magnetic field model. Which model, and whether the peak survives a second model during an extreme storm, is not in the material read.

The release links the peak to chorus waves through co-occurrence (intense chorus; plasmasphere eroded, recovery about 4.3-4.7 days vs about 2 typical). The same erosion changes plasmaspheric hiss, which the release itself names as a shaper of the barrier through scattering loss. Loss is not carried into the 'local gain' inference in the text read.
No uncertainties on PSD, peak height, or peak growth in the material read.
Event study of a natural storm; preregistration not expected.

averages.text: location of the impenetrable barrier (inner edge of multi-MeV electrons)
averages.estimated_from: storms observed before the 2014 discovery (Baker et al. 2014, not read); L = 2.8 is CALET's 'nominal' value
